reason: Weighty bills close periphery-center health gaps: insurance fee cuts, emergency rooms, hospitals and medical equipment in outlying towns. The statement and its examples match; ambulance deployment bills are close enough.

About two thirds of the weight is board quotas for women and representation targets or incentives for Arab, Haredi and disabled workers. General discrimination bans, harassment, pay, football fans and pensions are off.

statements.new_statement_en: Landlords should be free to raise rent and end leases as they choose, without legal limits, even if tenants have to move more often.

reason: Rent-increase caps are only about 40% of the weight; the fair-lease law, emergency and pandemic lease extensions also protect tenure. Broadened to cover ending leases. Broker fees and long-term leaseholds are off.

Weighty bills protect residents evacuated for earthquake strengthening, Kfar Shalem, Givat Amal and Abu Kabir clearance, and collapse-risk buildings with compensation. Matches. Limits on demolishing illegal Arab construction and West Bank holders are off.

Most weight raises penalties for sexual, violent, weapons, organized and property-related crimes, including attacks on specific victims. Matches. Tobacco enforcement, security-services regulation, procedural testimony rules and special police powers are off.

split.name_en: Limits on police force at protests
split.plus_en: Stricter rules on how police disperse protests and use force, with body cameras and accountability for police violence
split.minus_en: Police keep broad discretion to disperse assemblies and use force

split.name_en: State compensation for wrongful detention and prosecution
split.plus_en: Wider state liability to compensate people wrongly detained, shackled, prosecuted or later acquitted
split.minus_en: Narrower state liability for such compensation

reason: About 60% of the weight limits police force at protests (dispersal rules, body cameras, police violence), not compensation; compensation bills are about 30%. These are different positions. Kafr Qasim recognition is off.

The dominant bill (80% of weight) eases cooling-off for officials running in local elections; the rest lengthen cooling-off for regulators, judges and ministers. The statement covers both running for office and joining companies.

statements.new_statement_en: Elected officials and candidates should not be removed or barred from running over their views, even if they voice support for armed struggle against Israel.

reason: Expelling sitting members is under half the weight; the rest bars Knesset and local candidates (right to be elected, identity declaration, local elections law). Broadened to cover removal and barring candidates.

statements.new_statement_en: Fewer jobs should need a state license, and licenses should be easier to get, such as through shorter internships, even if professional standards may fall.

reason: Half the weight eases entry (bar exams, health-condition licensing, foreign providers); the other half creates new licensing regimes (security services, sports coaches, ship agents). Broadened to cover both. Rackets, gambling, domain registry are off.
Weighty bills change the number of ministers, deputy ministers and paid deputy mayors (the Basic Law: Government amendment dominates). Caps and the rotation-government repeal fit the statement.
Most weight is adopter eligibility, single-parent and couple adoption, and dropping the same-religion condition. Matches. Bills banning separation of siblings are off.

The weightiest bills ban payments from foreign states; side jobs, gifts and information misuse also fit. The many cooling-off bills (about 40%) belong to the separate cooling-off statement; city rabbis' discipline is off.
